nodes.label: docs/canon/USER_CANON.md — what the user actually said, verbatim, organised by subject: the design canon in 13 subjects, the working-relationship canon in 10, a dated timeline of decisions and reversals, and an inventory of what was never built and never answered. Interpretation, produced 2026-08-03, unreviewed: the quotes themselves are verbatim intent, but which quotes were selected, how they were grouped and what the headings call them are all agent judgement, and 141 entries are second-hand [DOC] recoveries rather than chat. Nothing is smoothed, corrected or paraphrased; where a section needs interpretation to be usable it appears on a line beginning Reading: and never inside a quote. Contradictions are preserved, not resolved — where he said one thing and later the opposite, both appear in date order and the reversal is named.

What this covers, and the source class every quote carries. Verbatim human turns: the corpus is 1,304, 2026-05-14T12:30:48Z → 2026-08-13T18:10:01Z, desktop 127 + laptop 1,177, merged — but this document's quote selection was made against the 803-turn snapshot that existed on 08-03 (desktop 127 + laptop 676), and the 501 turns added since are in the corpus and have not been swept into these sections. Second-hand recovered rulings: 80 labelled rulings plus ~150 verbatim quotes from 20 agent-written design docs, 05-25 → 07-12. Git: 74 commits, 2026-05-07 → 2026-08-01, 91 reproduce commands, 18 numbered contradictions. The source classes: [CHAT] — from raw/user_turns_all.jsonl, the user's own keystrokes, first-hand, timestamped, the primary source; [DOC] — recovered from an agent-written design/state doc that quoted him, second-hand and reliable to the extent that agent transcribed accurately; [COMMIT] — his own commit message, first-hand but terse; [TOOL-RESULT — absent from the corpus] — his answer to an AskUserQuestion prompt, quoted from the session transcript and cited by session file, record line and UTC timestamp, first-hand but not reachable through user_turns_all.jsonl because the extractor drops any record carrying a tool result.

What this canon cannot tell you. Nothing before 2026-05-14 exists as chat: the project's first commit is 2026-05-07, and the whole first week — the initial 52-file Neo4j pipeline, the 12-entry decision log, the original graph schema, the controlled canonical vocabulary — survives only in git and in the design docs, with no transcript anywhere. Two chat blackouts, 05-16 → 05-26 (11 days) and 05-29 → 06-26 (29 days), zero human turns on either machine, containing the entire v2 pivot, the facet redesign, the closing of the graph spine, the death of the chunk description, the build gate, the eval-harness design and the RAGAS-only purge — they are not lost, being covered second-hand by the [DOC] record (20 docs dated 05-25 through 07-12) and by git, so every [DOC] quote from those dates is the only surviving trace of that statement, and the claim that these windows "have no records of any kind" is wrong. Thin days are thin, not silent. And every answer he gave through an AskUserQuestion prompt is missing from the corpus, because tools/canon_extract.py discards a user record the moment it carries a tool_result block, before any text is extracted (2,530 records in the laptop pass) — so "there is no turn for it" does not mean he never said it. Four such records are named with their timestamps: 2026-07-30T23:10:40.745Z (how tags inform the interpretation), 2026-08-02T09:32:26.648Z (chunk position in cluster space; rank-aware metrics first), 2026-08-05T11:39:56.193Z (no framing — report the statistics), 2026-08-05T13:48:50.008Z (flag-gated derivation — "strange question and i dont get it").

The pre-chat era is in git — go read it. The design history of the blackout weeks is written down in commits, diffs, code and docs, and these are the design-era record 2026-05-07 → 2026-06-28: dba1160 (05-07) the initial commit, 52 files, the full Neo4j indexing pipeline, docs/architecture.md with its 12-entry decision log and the 280-line graph_schema.md; 48fbc9d (05-11) "rename cluster dimensions" → theme→topic, object_entity→entities, event_process→activity, time_relevance→temporal, information_need→evidence; 399ee32 (05-13) "Rework HERB chunking and tagging frames", which also silently deletes the canonical vocabulary; 415148d (05-14) the query interpretation layer and the pilot report; 4ab34b4 (05-15) the only commit that ever carried Claude memory files; 54bc1a4 (05-28) v1 as shipped, retrieval.ts with the seven-factor scoreCypher and its five hard gates; 296fc40 (05-30) the v2 artefact-rebuild design and shape-probe prototype; 18d11df (06-01) the reference-resolver prototype and the semantic-dimensions research; 0efff16 (06-15) "Separate repo into v1/ (frozen) and v2/ (active)", +750 design lines, the largest single design landing and the first CLAUDE.md; 28c95aa (06-24) the v3/artefact subsystem; 8a640bf (06-28) titled "update graphify-out (533 files)" but actually shipping the tagger and chunker and deleting v3/eval/herb.py; 69115e0 (07-12) titled "update graphify-out (49 files)" but actually introducing v3/pipelines/artefact_v1.py, the arm producing every reported artefact number; and origin/jockedev2 (05-19), six unmerged RAGAS commits squashed with an empty body, the only surviving record of "Effect is question-type-dependent — not a general graph win." The current branch has been cleared of old material: the working tree is not the record.

How to re-derive this: python tools/canon_extract.py, which writes docs/canon/raw/ — user_turns_all.jsonl / .md (the corpus), rejected_sample*.md (what the filter threw out and why), and EXTRACT_REPORT*.md (counts, per-rule reject tallies, and the false-negative audit of the harness_template rule: 0 of 6,380). The desktop half is merged in from the OneDrive _desktop_transcripts folder. docs/canon/raw/ is read-only: do not edit it, re-derive instead.

§1 the artefact's intended construction — the single fullest statement of the v1 concept in the record is his own 07-06 description of the shape: file → chunks → tags, the chunk carrying a short description and a relational weight to its file, the tags carrying relational values to their chunk, facet values on the tags, and "pretty much all of this is embedded"; with the interpreter doing its thing with the input — facet values and rankings of the prompt, and a description of the prompt which can be embedded and checked against chunk-description embeddings.

§2 the graph, and using it as a graph. The node/attribute rule in his own words, all [DOC] 06-12 — either they are nodes but then edges reach every chunk, or they are just attributes, and "perhaps it's smarter to just have shit like that as attributes on chunks" — against his [CHAT] 06-30 "i really think this should be nodes or edges so to speak etc, half the strength of of a graph is beeing able to route/search based on relationships instead of structures" and his 07-01 "having it as a rule to make nodes out of shared fields between files/areas etc.. Isn't that a generally useful concept? Dont think herb, think dataset agnostic concept". The question "is the graph actually being used as a graph?" is asked seven times across five weeks and never answered to his satisfaction.

§3 tags — what they are and what they are for. The purpose statement, said twice on the same day: "the whole fucking point of the tags, is guiding to the correct gold-bearing chunks" ([CHAT] 07-30). §3's reversal: "tags first" was said, then the implementation of it was rejected — on 07-30 he asked to make sure retrieval is informed by the tags first, and on 08-01, twelve minutes after a tag-reachability gate shipped, "ITS NT SUPPOSED TO BE FUCKING TAG REACHABLE ffs.. tags are supposed to INFORM/weight the chunks". The two are read as different mechanisms: weighting priority, not membership.

§4 facets. The origin statement: facets exist to "give the tag a more semantical weight and direction". Why the model cannot produce them, where they live, and what kind of thing a facet is — a definition that moved three times. The multi-step relevance concept, 06-27: the facet weight in combination with the tag's chunk-relevance weight tells how relevant the tag actually is in relation to the prompt, based on the interpreter's evaluation of which facets are most relevant for the input. A mechanism he floated himself. Objections to combining them, none of them a ruling. Then five weeks of asking what the facets are actually doing (07-20 "how the fuck are facets used here then?", 07-21 "how did we get the facet-values now?", 07-25 "what is affecting the interpreter from the facets") with no answer he accepted in the record.

§4 THE FACET REVERSALS — three of them, all his own. F1, what a facet is: three positions, each killing the one before — 06-14 a relevance coordinate of a tag ("relevance weights, not interpretation"), 06-25 semantic meaning around the tag with routing separate ("the v1 facets were actual semantic meaning around the tag"), 06-27 a graded how-much dial ("you HAVE to remember that the facets are themed RELEVANCE weights.. meaninig you have to think about them differently, like info-kind and entity-type (are they even facets..?)") — the third ending in his own open question. F2, entity-type and information-kind: out (05-30), back in (06-25), out again (06-27), with the reconciliation against the 06-28 categorical framing recorded as an open problem that was never closed.

§5 clustering, cluster-K, levels of k's, fuzzy cutoffs. The pre-v1 instinct of clustering on facets as a filter/router; 07-21 "clustering IS embedding distances against each other", not rankings or countings, and "the clusters are based on the actual shit from the prompt, so you cant pre-run it..?"; 07-22 the curve of best fit decides the correct K per query; 07-31 the fullest specification — "i THINK it might be smartest to compute the clusters at build, and then weight-adjust them based on the query's facet-values.. i THINK, reflect on this with me", "i used best fit as the fuzzy cutoff-point for the cluster's edges tho … perhaps the query-adjustment comes first", and "the original thought was … clustering of tags weighted by facets, meaning each type of facet was a separate sort of clustering to get semantically different clusters".

§5 Reading — the vocabulary, and who owns which word. Fuzzy clustering, levels of k's and query-relative areas are the user's own terms; gap cut, NNK and RRF fusion are agent translations he never named — 07-20 "NONE of these are something i named or invented, what the fuck are they?" — and the audit measures the rest: levels of k's yes, areas marginal, while walk, anchor, stated-scope, support and parts are agent text or him echoing it back.

§6 retrieval shape — guidance, not filtering. The four-point rejection of the gate, [CHAT] 07-15: "gate? wtf? why have a gate? why not ust that as promoted guidance? … hard filter seems insane, much better to use rankings etc", and in the same exchange "2. 10? fucking why just 10? … Honestly, no fucking wonder we get shit results, this is an abomination". The rule binds every later mechanism: a signal weights and ranks, it never excludes.

§7 arbitrary numbers. The rule, [CHAT] 07-15: "i do NOT like arbitrary choices for k or any number or value, fucking BASE it on something, i kinda like knn clustering for relevance spheres for example for grounding, k, retrival etc etc"; restated 07-21 "why did you make up a number like 200 here?" and 08-02 "arbitrarily decided hard limits, like the 64 chunk limit, i bet there is way more than 1 of these dumb limits lying around not beeing seen".

§8 overfitting, and keeping agents blind to the gold. "by NOT overfitting it to the specific dataset we have" (06-30), restated 07-15 and 07-22; then 08-02, the access cut: "honestly, you should not have the questions/gold available to you, there is 0% good that can come out of taht" and "can we make sure 'you' never see them? that you only get the variable/pointer to it?".

§9 evaluation, metrics, and what the score is and is not for: the scorer decision and its reversal seven days later; the standing rulings; gathering the data (06-27 "gather ALL the data for the named k's", no interpretation and no curve substitutes); the benchmark itself; matched budget and the unit problem, which he found himself on 07-26 — "k=50 does not mean the same for all arms, and thats retarded" and "perhaps K shouldnt be chunks, perhaps we should put a max token budget instead"; the 90%-air problem (07-29 "we find pretty much all gold, but also 90% air"); held-out generalization on his terms; and judges and generators.
§9 what the score is NOT for — the clearest statement in the whole record, [CHAT] 07-25: the point is an academically valid artefact, not chasing the highest number.

§10–13. §10 aggregation and multi-hop: "but, doesnt the graph give actual relational connections to things like this, i mean, if the 'name' example you had, why wouldnt if just find all of those names? i dont get it", and "if we build the graph correctly, wont it emulate/do multihop natively purely by design?". §11 relationships and hub nodes — the 06-30 nodes-or-edges statement against the 08-02 rejection "dude, you are turbo-overfitting now, AND doing shit that might as well be sql-schema", all three positions his and none retired. §12 generalization beyond HERB: "Dont think herb, think dataset agnostic concept" (07-01) against "there is only HERB dataset, forget everything else" (07-15). §13 weights — measured, never emitted.

PART II — the working-relationship canon, §14–23. §14 do not manufacture canon: naming a thing does not make it canon, and text in the repo is not his approval of it. §15 an opinion is not a command; a question is not a work order — a question he asks is recorded as the question it is. §16 communication: plain spoken English, short answers, no internal doc ids. §17 he runs the scripts and the terminal must show life. §18 usage is finite and he pays for it. §19 reusable tools, not a new script per experiment. §20 delegation and adversarial review: orchestrator mode, permanent specialist agents, blind panels. §21 read the actual thing — code, git, repo — not a summary of it: "THE GODDAMN GIT REPO HAS ALL THE FUCKING HISTORY SPOKEN IN COMMITS, DIFFS, CODE and DOCS". §22 repo, commits, and what must never be thrown away. §23 machine and environment facts he stated himself.
PART III — the dated timeline of decisions and reversals, one quote-anchored line each with ↺ marking a reversal, running from the first surviving chat to the record's end.

PART IV — never built, never answered. A. Specified in detail, designed, never built: the aggregation path, the relationships / hub-node layer, pass 2 in its entirety with the exponential curve, per-facet channels, centrality, chunk attribute extraction, the fuzzy-embedding pre-pass, the gold-blindness mechanism. B. The three falsifiers — the ~30-phrase orthogonality probe, the per-dial divergence check, the channel-blend reorder test — each gating a layer, none run. C. Constants nobody based on anything. D. Adopted then silently un-adopted with no reversal recorded anywhere. E. Asked and never answered. F. Open at the moment this record ends (2026-08-03).

How to use this file. A quote is evidence, a summary is not: if you are about to state what he wants, find the quote first and cite it; where two of his quotes conflict, both stand and no agent picks a winner; a conflict between the record and what you believe is correct is raised as a question in the conversation, never resolved silently.
